_status: DRAFT prose for make_rural_page.py, written from metrics.json, data/robustness_dates.json and the subagent's check of the images.
scene_credit: Sentinel-2B scene of 21 Feb 2019 and Sentinel-2C scene of 19 Feb 2026, tile 43PFQ
lede: Two cloud-free Sentinel-2 satellite pictures of Assembly constituency 197 in Hassan district are compared pixel by pixel at 10 m. They were taken two days apart in the calendar, seven years apart: 21 February 2019 and 19 February 2026. This is the third constituency in a series that covers a seat held by each of the three main parties. It measures land cover only and says nothing about who caused any change.
warning_title: Read this first: the change here is mostly a wet year against a dry one.
warning: Holenarasipur is farmland and tanks. On the 30 clean dates checked, green cover moved 7 to 10 points within a single February. Around 19 to 21 February it stood at 34% in 2019, 47% in 2025 and 41% in 2026. 2026 was greener and less bare than 2019 on every matched pair of dates, by 8 to 25 points, so the direction holds; the pair used below shows the smallest gap of all. That fits a dry 2018-19 season and a wet 2025-26 one. Do not quote the tiles below as land restored. The fuller tanks are real for that date, but tanks fill and empty with each monsoon.
chart_title: Is the change real? Green cover on every clean date, January to March
chart_note: Share of the constituency with NDVI above 0.4, computed at 20 m on every Sentinel-2 date with less than 1% cloud inside the boundary (tile 43PFQ). Large dots are the two dates used for the tiles and maps. The gap between years is mostly how wet the previous monsoon was.
change_caption: Most of the green lost and new red is farmland between harvest and sowing.
forest_note: OpenStreetMap maps only about 588 ha of forest here and no protected area, so this split says little.
limits: One picture per year, in the dry season. Green cover changes week by week; the date check above shows how much.
The bare or built-up figure is a proxy. In this rural seat it is mostly bare soil, harvested fields and dry grass, so its fall says nothing about buildings.
The two years use different satellites (Sentinel-2B and 2C) and processing versions. The -1000 reflectance offset for products processed from 2022 was applied.
Thresholds are standard textbook values, not tuned for Karnataka. Trust the direction of change more than the exact hectares.
10 m pixels blur roads, tree lines and small tanks. Water bodies under 2 ha are not measured; most tanks here are unnamed in OpenStreetMap and are listed by their map id.

The boundary is DataMeet's digitised map of the 2008 constituencies. Here it has a second, 105 ha piece just north of the main area, which may be a digitising error. Check edges against the official map before using any figure near them.
